Refine to GO:1900182, which does not require distinguishing import from nuclear retention. PANC-1, DLD1 and HK-2 recipient cells are human, but the commercial collagen reagent species and isolated alpha-1-chain contribution are not specified. Keep this contextual effect outside the structural core.

current_definitions.label: collagen binding
current_definitions.definition: Binding to collagen, a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals. response_assessments.scope: The current rat source measures developmental gene-expression changes under vitamin-A deficiency. This supports a context-dependent collagen expression response, not a separate COL1A1 nutrient-sensing molecular activity. Human transfer remains the original Ensembl inference.

The rat doxazosin study reports time-dependent collagen-I expression and prostate matrix changes. This supports the current donor response annotation at a tissue-response level, not xenobiotic metabolism or direct drug binding by human collagen.

Rat cardiac-fibroblast stretch and unloading/reloading studies connect mechanical conditions to collagen transcription or tissue deposition. The original orthology assertion is preserved; those readouts do not independently make COL1A1 a force sensor.

The complete rat high-fat-diet abstract reports reduced skin collagen-I RNA and protein. Retain the original response context without turning it into an independent nutrient-sensing function of human COL1A1.

The current rat Col1a1 source points to PMID:2456904, whose complete abstract explicitly identifies alpha-2(I), alpha-1(III) and alpha-2(V) collagen transcripts. Full experimental text was not recovered, so alpha-1(I) support cannot be verified from the abstract. Preserve the original inference as undecided, not as a disproven response or a confident wrong-gene claim.

The rat diabetic-bone study reports reduced collagen expression and reversal by insulin treatment. This supports the original expression-response inference, not insulin binding or an autonomous signaling activity of COL1A1.

The rat stellate-cell source links hydrogen peroxide/TGF-beta conditions to COL1A1 promoter and expression changes. This preserves the curated response without assigning peroxide catalysis, sensing or a separate oxidative-stress core to collagen.

The donor study uses a rat Col1a1 promoter in transgenic mouse calvarial cultures and reports PTH/cAMP regulation of promoter activity and collagen synthesis. Preserve the experimental construct/species boundary and original transfer; no direct hormone binding by collagen is inferred.

The rat calvarial-cell abstract reports long-term FGF2-associated changes in COL1 expression during osteoblast culture. It supports the preserved response context, not FGF receptor activity of COL1A1.

The rat anabolic-steroid/tendon study reports collagen expression changes under the tested treatment and training conditions. This is a response-associated matrix readout rather than steroid binding or signaling catalysis by human COL1A1.

The donor experiment couples PTH/cAMP treatment to rat Col1a1 promoter activity in transgenic mouse calvariae and to collagen synthesis. It does not show cAMP binding by the collagen protein. The original electronic annotation is preserved at this response scope.

The rat ligament study connects hyperbaric oxygen treatment to collagen expression and healing-associated matrix deposition. Retain the existing response annotation without assigning oxygen-sensing or catalytic activity to human collagen.

Current rat and mouse sources include loaded tendon-cell cultures and tenogenic/osteogenic expression readouts. COL1A1 is measured as an expression/matrix marker; this is not a direct demonstration of a collagen mechanosensor. Combined electronic identities are preserved.

Rat fetal-lung and hepatic-stellate-cell abstracts report altered collagen synthesis, chain ratios or COL1 expression after retinoid treatment. Preserve those response contexts and their original orthology inference without claiming direct retinoid binding by COL1A1.

The complete rat-chondrocyte abstract reports reduced Col1a1 expression during vitamin-E protection, alongside increased Agc1/Col2a1 expression and proteoglycan, viability and differentiation readouts. It establishes a transcriptional response, but does not establish alpha1(I) collagen as a component performing that protective response. Mark the participation inference as over-annotated at this source scope. Preserve the positive IEP donor result and the abstract-only access limit; no universal absence of collagen involvement is asserted.

The current rat donor assigns Col1a1 by IEP. In the original publisher Figure 4, high-glucose NRK-52E cells show increased collagen-I immunofluorescence and a collagen-I immunoblot band, reduced by Lefty-1 relative to the high-glucose and vector controls. This supports the type-I matrix-production response and the preserved contextual annotation. Full Methods and the antibody chain specificity were not recovered, so the exact alpha-1 assignment remains curator supplied; no human glucose-sensing activity or independent osmolarity control is claimed.

The rat stellate-cell abstract reports TNF-alpha/glutathione-linked suppression of COL1 expression. It supports the preserved cellular-response context without assigning TNF receptor or redox enzyme activity to COL1A1.

The rat fetal-lung study reports reduced collagen production and altered chain/trimer ratios after EGF exposure. Keep the original expression-response inference separate from EGF binding or receptor activity of the collagen protein.

Actual rat cardiac-fibroblast Methods/Results in PMID:23560091 measure COL1A1 RNA, cell-associated collagen, secreted collagen and promoter methylation after TGF-beta treatment. The second donor reference foregrounds COL1A2 and remains unresolved for the alpha-1-specific link; the directly verified source independently supports the contextual response.

The complete rat-skin abstract reports reduced Col1a1 RNA in males after six months of fluoride exposure, but no corresponding effect on the measured collagen-form concentrations or chain ratios. The positive expression result is preserved; inferring collagen-product participation from it exceeds the demonstrated response, so mark this source-specific inference as over-annotated. This is not a claim that COL1A1 cannot respond to fluoride. The separate osteoblast source with reduced type-I protein output remains distinct.

The rat osteoblast source specifically reports COL1A1 mRNA/protein reduction, distinct from COL1A2, under the tested fluoride condition. This supports the original response inference, not direct fluoride recognition by collagen.

The rat hepatic-stellate-cell abstract reports collagen-I expression under acetaldehyde/leptin conditions; the negative leptin synergy result is not converted into an absence of the acetaldehyde response. Keep this contextual transcriptional response separate from acetaldehyde metabolism or sensing by COL1A1.

response_guidance.scope: Differential expression alone need not establish product participation. Nineteen existing matrix-response contexts remain non-core; vitamin-E marker and rat-skin fluoride transcript-only inferences are over-annotated, and the exact estradiol donor relationship is unresolved. No automatic IEP acceptance or rejection and no response NEW.
